senses.definition: To leave a person, place, or thing permanently, especially when you have a duty to stay.
examples: The crew had to abandon the sinking ship.
She was abandoned by her business partners when the money ran out.
They abandoned the car at the side of the motorway.

senses.definition: To stop doing something before it is finished, usually because it is no longer possible or worthwhile.
examples: The search was abandoned after three days.
He abandoned his plan to study medicine.

note: A classic stress-shift difference: British English stresses the second syllable, American English the third.

senses.definition: A picture, short film, song, or text that tries to persuade people to buy a product or service.
examples: They placed an advertisement for the job in the local paper.
The advertisement claims the cream removes wrinkles in a week.
I first heard about the festival from an advertisement on the radio.

senses.definition: Something you say or write in reply to a question, letter, or situation.
examples: I asked her twice, but I never got an answer.
There is no simple answer to the housing crisis.

senses.definition: To say or write something in reply.
examples: Please answer the question honestly.
Nobody answered the door, so I left the parcel on the step.

senses.definition: A small, round, orange-yellow fruit with a stone in the middle.
examples: She picked a ripe apricot from the tree.
The tart was filled with apricot jam.
Dried apricots are a good source of fibre.

senses.definition: To say something to someone in order to get an answer or information.
examples: Can I ask you a personal question?
He asked the waiter for the bill.
If you are lost, ask someone for directions.

senses.definition: To request something, or to request that someone do something.
examples: She asked her neighbour to water the plants.
They are asking £300,000 for the flat.

senses.definition: A large container that you fill with water and sit in to wash your body; also the act of washing this way.
examples: I had a long, hot bath after the hike.
Could you run a bath for the children?
The old house still has a cast-iron bath.

note: In American English the /t/ between vowels is usually a quick tap, shown here as t̬.

senses.definition: Very pleasing to look at, listen to, or think about.
examples: The view from the summit was beautiful.
She has a beautiful singing voice.
It was a beautiful piece of reasoning, simple and complete.

senses.definition: For the reason that; used to introduce the cause of something.
examples: We stayed indoors because it was raining.
She was late because her train was cancelled.
I said no, because I simply did not have the time.

senses.definition: Of a higher standard or quality than something else; the comparative form of good.
examples: This translation is much better than the first one.
Is there a better route to avoid the traffic?

senses.definition: Healthier or less ill than before.
examples: I felt better after a night's sleep.
She is getting better, but slowly.

senses.definition: To take and use something belonging to someone else, intending to give it back.
examples: Can I borrow your charger for ten minutes?
He borrowed the money from his brother and paid it back in March.
You can borrow up to six books at a time from the library.

senses.definition: A group of people or things that share particular qualities and are considered together.
examples: The film won in three categories, including best score.
These expenses fall into a different category.
Applicants are sorted into four broad categories.

senses.definition: An occasion that makes it possible to do something; an opportunity.
examples: This is your last chance to change your mind.
I never had the chance to thank her properly.

senses.definition: The level of possibility that something will happen.
examples: There is a good chance of snow tonight.
The odds were against us, but we took the chance anyway.

note: British English rhymes this with 'park'; American English rhymes it with 'work'.

senses.definition: A person who works in an office, shop, or court keeping records or dealing with customers.
examples: The clerk stamped my form and handed it back.
She worked as a bank clerk before training as an accountant.
Ask the desk clerk for a spare key.

senses.definition: Making you feel physically relaxed and free from pain or tightness.
examples: These shoes are surprisingly comfortable.
Make yourself comfortable while I finish the call.

senses.definition: Confident and free from worry about a situation.
examples: I am not comfortable signing this without a lawyer.
He seems comfortable speaking to large audiences.

note: Many British speakers also say kənˈtrɒv.ə.si, with stress on the second syllable.

senses.definition: A lot of public disagreement or argument about something that many people feel strongly about.
examples: The decision caused considerable controversy among staff.
The painting has been the subject of controversy since it was bought.
He resigned after weeks of controversy over his expenses.
